BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r4.claim: Samk means height or an elevated structure; the heavens are called al-masmūkāt for their height, and ʿAlī's prayer and al-Farazdaq's line illustrate the term.
JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r4.anchor: ومنه حديث علي: يا بارئ السبع المسموكات، ويقال: سنام سامك

JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r5.speaker: الفرزدق
JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r5.claim: His line “the One who raised the sky built for us a house” uses samaka for raising or making high.
JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r5.anchor: وقال الفرزدق: إن الذي سمك السماء بنى لنا ... بيتا دعائمه أعز وأطول

JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r6.claim: The opposite of height is depth; samk is construction above, while depth is below.
JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r6.anchor: ونقيض السمك: العمق، والسمك: البناء في العلو، والعمق في السفل

JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r7.claim: Taswiya means making one thing match another in its form and meaning.
JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r7.anchor: والتسوية: جعل أحد الشيئين على مقدار الآخر في نفسه ومعناه

TABATABAI:79:27-34/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:27-34/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:27-34/r5.claim: Heaven's raised height is its elevated ceiling; its leveling arranges and places each part according to wisdom, as in 38:72.
TABATABAI:79:27-34/r5.anchor: أي رفع سقفها وما ارتفع منها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:27-34/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:27-34/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:27-34/r2.claim: God raised the heaven's roof and made it even, without cracks or fissures.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:27-34/r2.anchor: { رفع سمكها } سقفها { فسواها } بلا شقوق ولا فطور

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r9.claim: God built the heaven, raised its roof, and made it even, without seams, cracks, or breaks.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r9.anchor: {رفع سمكها} سقفها {فسواها} بلا شطور [ولا شقوق] (3) ولا فطور.

NAHHAS:v5p143/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p143/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p143/r18.claim: The sky is described as a roof over the earth.

SAMIN-DURR:79:28/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:28/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:28/r1.claim: رفع سمكها explains the manner of the building; سمك means height or elevation.
SAMIN-DURR:79:28/r1.anchor: قوله: { رفع سمكها }: جملة مفسرة لكيفية البناء. والسمك: الارتفاع.

SAMIN-DURR:79:28/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:28/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:79:28/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the phrase as making the heaven’s extent in the direction of height vast and lofty.
SAMIN-DURR:79:28/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " جعل مقدار ذهابها في سمت العلو مديدا رفعيا "

SAMIN-DURR:79:28/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:28/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:28/r3.claim: سمك الشيء means raise it into the air, while سمك هو means rise; سنام سامك means high and elevated, illustrating transitive and intransitive uses.
SAMIN-DURR:79:28/r3.anchor: وسمكت الشيء: رفعته في الهواء. وسمك هو، أي: ارتفع سموكا فهو قاصر ومتعد

SAMIN-DURR:79:28/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:28/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:28/r4.claim: سماك البيت is what supports a raised house; al-Simāk is the name of two stars, Rāmiḥ and Aʿzal. An unnamed poet uses سمك for raising the heaven.
SAMIN-DURR:79:28/r4.anchor: إن الذي سمك السماء بنى لنا بيتا دعائمه أعز وأطول

ASAD-NOTES:79:27#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:79:27#n13/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:79:27#n13/r1.claim: Asad says 87:2 is the earliest instance in revelation chronology of sawwa used in this sense.
ASAD-NOTES:79:27#n13/r1.anchor: the earliest instance, in the chronology of Qur'anic revelation, of the use of the verb sawwa in the above sense.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r1.claim: Samk is the sky's height above the earth toward the upper direction; it may also mean thickness, whose upper-to-lower measure is called depth.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r1.anchor: جعل مقدار ارتفاعها من الأرض وذهابها إلى سمت العلو مديدا رفيعا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r2.claim: Sound reports give five hundred years of travel between earth and the lowest heaven, and likewise between heavens and for each heaven's thickness; he takes the measure literally as customary travel and a definite number.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r2.anchor: جاء في الأخبار الصحيحة أن ارتفاع السماء الدنيا عن الأرض خمسمائة عام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r3.claim: God made the heaven even in accordance with wisdom, leaving no part without what its wisdom requires, including adornment with stars.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r3.anchor: جعلها سواء فيما اقتضته الحكمة فلم يخل عز وجل قطعة منها عما تقتضيه الحكمة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r4.claim: One explanation takes making it even to mean smoothing its surface so it has no rises or depressions.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r4.anchor: وقيل تسويتها جعلها ملساء ليس في سطحها انخفاض وارتفاع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r5.speaker: كثير
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r5.claim: Another view says the heavens have simple, similar parts and a genuinely spherical form; many scholars held this, citing their created dependence on a freely choosing maker and seeing no religious harm in sphericity.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r5.anchor: وإليه ذهب كثير وقالوا وحكاه الإمام لما ثبت أنها محدثة مفتقرة إلى فاعل مختار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r6.claim: A further view reads the phrase as completing the heavens with stars, celestial accessories, and epicycles; al-Alusi says this rests on an early-unattested identification of heavens with spheres and on weak astronomical proofs, so the truth is left to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#3/r6.anchor: هذا مع بنائه على اتحاد السماوات والأفلاك غير معروف في الصدر الأول من المسلمين

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r3.claim: Samk is either its height above the earth or its thickness, made loftily extended.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r3.anchor: أي جعل مقدار ارتفاعها من الأرض أو ثخنها لذاهب في العلو رفيعا

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r4.claim: He leveled it, made it even, or completed it with stars, celestial spheres, and other features; the word can mean setting something right.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r4.anchor: فعدلها أو فجعلها مستوية، أو فتممها بما يتم به كمالها من الكواكب والتداوير وغيرها

BINTSHATI:v1p150/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r2.claim: The cosmic signs are framed as a question so deniers will answer themselves; reflection shows that recreating decayed bones is no harder than creating heaven.
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r2.anchor: وقد ساق القرآن هذه الآيات بأسلوب الاستفهام ليرجعوا إلى أنفسهم فيلتمسوا جواب ما سئلوا عنه

BINTSHATI:v1p150/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r3.claim: The heaven's vast height, unreachable and unsupported by visible columns, dwarfs the familiar human buildings that need reachable materials and supports.
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r3.anchor: وأين ذلك كله من تلك السماء، في ارتفاعها الشاهق الذي لا مجال لبلوغه، وفي قيامها على غير عمد ترى

BINTSHATI:v1p150/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r4.anchor: والسمك: القامة والعلو. وتكلف مفسرون فحددوا مقدار ذلك السمك

BINTSHATI:v1p150/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r5.speaker: مفسرون في الكشاف والبحر
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r5.claim: Some commentators set heaven's height at five hundred years.
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r5.anchor: جعل مقدارها في العلو مديداً رفيعاً، مقدار خمسمائة عامّ

BINTSHATI:v1p150/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r6.claim: Bint al-Shati rejects the five-hundred-year measure as unsupported by the text and unlike Qur'anic descriptions of cosmic signs; measures tied to travel speed change across eras.
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r6.anchor: وهذا ما لا يقبله النص من قريب ولا بعيد، كما أنه ليس من مألوف البيان القرآني

BINTSHATI:v1p150/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r7.speaker: محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r7.claim: Muhammad Abduh reads raising the heaven's height as raising the heavenly bodies above us; the author finds this unpersuasive.
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r7.anchor: وذهب الشيخ محمد عبده إلى أن رفع السمك هنا هو

BINTSHATI:v1p150/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r8.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r8.claim: Taswiya denotes straightness, balance, and equilibrium.
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r8.anchor: أما التسوية - وهي في اللغة استقامة واعتدال وإتزان

BINTSHATI:v1p150/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r9.speaker: مفسرون
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r9.claim: Commentators explain taswiya as completing and repairing, making the heaven smooth and even, and executing its construction with precision; the author accepts these close senses as textually possible without strain.
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r9.anchor: فمن المفسرين من تأولها هنا بالتتميم وبالإصلاح

BINTSHATI:v1p150/r10.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r10.speaker: محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r10.claim: Abduh says taswiya means placing each heavenly body in its proper position; the author rejects this as a poor fit for the Qur'anic sense of evenness and precision.
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r10.anchor: وأما قول الشيخ محمد عبده إن التسوية هي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r10.speaker: القاموس
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r10.claim: Al-Qāmūs gives samk as a roof, the span from a house’s top to bottom, or the stature of anything.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r10.anchor: قال في القاموس : السمك السقف , أو من أعلى البيت إلى أسفله , أو القامة من كل شيء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r11.speaker: أبو حيان
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r11.claim: Abū Ḥayyān defines samk as the height between the sky’s near surface and the surface above it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r11.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : السمك الارتفاع الذي بين سطح السماء الذي يلينا وسطحها الذي يلي ما فوقها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r12.claim: God raised the sky’s height and made it even, without higher or lower parts or cracks, completing it with stars and other features.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r12.anchor: عدلها عقب ذلك بأن جعلها مستوية لا شيء فيها أعلى من شيء ولا أخفض ولا فطور فيها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r13.claim: He proportioned the thicknesses of each heaven and earth and the spaces between them so none exceeds another.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r13.anchor: وجعل مقدار تخن كل سماء وما بين كل سماءين وتخن كل أرض وما بين كل أرضين على السواء

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3398#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3398#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3398#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains raising its height as building it.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3398#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : رفع سمكها قال : بناها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#3/r1.claim: God raised the heaven’s height and loftiness into the air and made it even, without rifts, cracks, or differences in elevation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#3/r1.anchor: ومعنى رفع سمكها رفع ارتفاعها وعلوها في الهواء فسواها بلا شقوق ولا فطور ولا تفاوت يرتفع فيه بعضها على بعض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r4.claim: God built the sky by raising it high, extending and leveling it, and adorning it with stars.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r4.anchor: فقوله: {بناها} فسره بقوله: {رفع سمكها فسواها} أي: جعلها عالية البناء، بعيدة الفناء، مستوية الأرجاء، مكللة بالكواكب في الليلة الظلماء.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r2.claim: God built the heaven by raising its height to a vast expanse, described as a journey of five hundred years upward.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r2.anchor: { رفع سمكها } أي جعل مقدار ذهابها في سمت العلو مديدا رفيعا مسيرة خمسمائة عام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r3.claim: One explanation says He made the heaven even and smooth, with no disparity or fissures; another says He completed and set it right as needed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r3.anchor: { فسواها } فعدلها مستوية ملساء ، ليس فيها تفاوت ولا فطور . أو فتممها بما علم أنها تتم به

MUJAHID:v2p728/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p728/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p728/r1.claim: Mujahid explains the raised height of the sky as its structure, built without pillars.
MUJAHID:v2p728/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ رفع سمكها ﴾ يعني بنيانها بغير عمد

MUQATIL:79:27-33/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:27-33/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:27-33/r3.claim: The sky's height is a journey of five hundred years.
MUQATIL:79:27-33/r3.anchor: يعني طولها مسيرة خمسمائة عام { فسواها }

MUQATIL:79:27-33/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:27-33/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:27-33/r4.claim: God fashioned the sky without any flaw.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#6/r1.claim: He raised the sky's roof high.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#6/r1.anchor: ﴿ رفع سمكها ﴾ أعلى سقفها وقيل جعل مقدار

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#6/r2.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#6/r2.claim: An alternative explanation says its vertical extent is immense, a distance of five hundred years.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#6/r2.anchor: وقيل جعل مقدار ذهابها فى سمت العلو رفيعا مسيرة خمسمائة عام

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#6/r3.claim: He made the sky even, with no cracks or fissures.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#6/r3.anchor: ﴿ فسواها ﴾ فعدلها مستوية بلا شقوق ولا فطور

BURSEVI:v10p252/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p252/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p252/r1.claim: This explains the building: God made the sky’s rise from earth into the heights vast, a distance of five hundred years’ journey.
BURSEVI:v10p252/r1.anchor: بيان للبناء أي جعل مقدار ارتفاعها من الأرض وذهابها إلى سمت العلو

BURSEVI:v10p252/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p252/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p252/r2.claim: Another view defines samk as the sky’s thickness, the distance between its lower and upper surfaces, likewise a five-hundred-year journey.
BURSEVI:v10p252/r2.anchor: السمك الارتفاع الذي بين سطح السماء الأسفل الذي يلينا وسطحها الأعلى

QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r4.claim: Samk means height: God lifted heaven's roof into the air; samakta means raising something aloft.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r4.anchor: { رفع سمكها } أي أعلى سقفها في الهواء يقال: سمكت الشيء

QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r5.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r5.claim: Al-Farraʾ says anything that supports another thing is called samk; related forms describe high buildings and camel humps.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء: كل شيء حمل شيئا من البناء وغيره فهو سمك. وبناء مسموك وسنام سامك تامك أي عال

QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r6.claim: Al-masmukat names the heavens, and asmiq fi al-daym means climb a degree.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r6.anchor: والمسموكات: السموات. ويقال: اسمك في الديم، أي اصعد في الدرجة.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r7.claim: God fashioned heaven proportionately, without unevenness, cracks, or fissures.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r7.anchor: أي خلقها خلقا مستويا، لا تفاوت فيه، ولا شقوق، ولا فطور.

RAZI-FULL:v31p43/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p43/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p43/r1.claim: After stating that God built heaven, the passage turns to explain how He built it.
RAZI-FULL:v31p43/r1.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى لما بين في السماء أنه بناها

RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r1.claim: A thing’s extent measured from top to bottom is its depth, while its extent from bottom to top is its height (samk).
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r1.anchor: إذا أخذ من أعلاه إلى أسفله سمي عمقا

RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r2.claim: The phrase means that heaven is extremely high; some report that earth and heaven are separated by a journey of five hundred years.
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r2.anchor: فالمراد برفع سمكها شدة علوها حتى ذكروا أن ما بين الأرض وبينها مسيرة خمسمائة عام

RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r3.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r3.claim: Others understand the phrase as heaven being raised without pillars, something only God can accomplish.
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل المراد : رفع سمكها من غير عمد

RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r4.claim: One interpretation takes “He leveled it” to mean that God composed and proportioned heaven.

RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r5.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes the phrase to mean that heaven has no cracks, as in the statement that one sees no disparity in the Merciful’s creation.
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : بل المراد نفي الشقوق عنها

RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r6.speaker: القائلون بالقول الأول
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r6.claim: Advocates of the first view say the unqualified wording means complete proportion: heaven must be spherical, since other shapes have edges and unequal distances; its sphericity poses no religious harm.

RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r7.speaker: أصحاب الهيئة
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r7.claim: Astronomers have calculated the sizes of celestial bodies and the distances from each to earth.
RAZI-FULL:v31p43#2/r7.anchor: بين أصحاب الهيئة مقادير الأجرام الفلكية وأبعاد

STUDYQURAN:79:28/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:28/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:28/r1.claim: The sky, its night and day, and the spread earth are further dimensions of creation demonstrating God's power to create and resurrect.
STUDYQURAN:79:28/r1.anchor: These verses describe additional dimensions of creation, which demonstrate that God can create and resurrect as He will.

STUDYQURAN:79:28/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:28/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:28/r2.claim: The sky's canopy refers to its highest level.
STUDYQURAN:79:28/r2.anchor: Its canopy indicates the highest level of the sky

STUDYQURAN:79:28/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:28/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:28/r3.claim: Fashioning the sky means making it whole, without fissures, cracks, or imperfections; its perfection is linked to 67:3–4.
STUDYQURAN:79:28/r3.anchor: fashioned it implies that it is whole with no fissures, cracks, or imperfections

TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r3.claim: Heaven was leveled so that no part is higher or lower than another and its height and extent are even.
TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r3.anchor: فسوى السماء، فلا شيء أرفع من شيء، ولا شيء أخفض من شيء

TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r4.claim: Qatāda explains the phrase as raising the structure of heaven and making it even.

TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid says its structure was raised without pillars.

TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses its samk as its construction.

THALABI:v10p127/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p127/r10.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v10p127/r10.claim: Al-Farra says samk is anything that carries or supports a structure or other thing; the related forms are samk, bināʾ, and sumūk.
THALABI:v10p127/r10.anchor: قال الفراء: كل شيء حمل شيئا من البناء وغيره فهو سمك وبناء وسموك

THALABI:v10p127/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p127/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p127/r11.claim: God made the heaven even, without divisions or cracks.

ELMALILI:79:27-33/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r4.claim: God raised heaven to a great height without pillars.
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r4.anchor: boyuna irtifâ‘verdi direksiz olarak yükseğe[^1] kaldırdı.

ELMALILI:79:27-33/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r5.claim: Semk is a thing’s height or vertical extension from bottom upward; considered from above downward it is called umq. Some also explain it as thickness in breadth and length.
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r5.anchor: “Semk” bir şeyin “irtifâ‘” tâbir ettiğimiz boyu, aşağıdan yukarıya imtidâdı ve yüksekliğidir.

ELMALILI:79:27-33/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r6.claim: Heaven was balanced, ordered, and set right, as in the verse saying God raised heaven and established the balance.
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r6.anchor: mîzânını vaz‘edip denkleştirdi, nizâmına koyup düzeltti.

ELMALILI:79:27-33/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r7.claim: Elmalılı rejects the inference that this wording proves the entire heaven has a perfect spherical form; that overall shape is not established, and its detail is known to God.
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r7.anchor: bütün semânın hey’et-i umûmiyesinin şekli tam küre olduğu sâbit değildir. Tafsîlini Allah bilir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r1.claim: The vast, complex, ordered cosmos is evidence to resurrection deniers that its creator can raise people again; another verse says creating heaven and earth is greater than creating humanity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r1.anchor: böylesine geniş ve kompleks olan, düzenli ve uyumlu işleyen varlıklar dünyasını yaratan kudretin insanları da öldükten sonra tekrar diriltebileceğine işaret edilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r2.claim: God's creation of the heavens without pillars is among the signs of His limitless power and ability to resurrect.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r3.claim: Making night pitch dark and day bright is among the signs of God's limitless power and ability to resurrect.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r3.anchor: geceyi zifiri karanlık, gündüzü ise aydınlık kılması (Bakara 2/164; Nebe’ 78/10-11)

ITQAN:v2p336#3/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p336#3/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p336#3/r4.claim: The noun samk means the sky's construction or height.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r5.speaker: قالوا
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r5.claim: They argue that Fussilat places the earth's creation before the heavens, whereas al-Naziat appears to place the heaven's construction before the earth's spreading.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r5.anchor: وقال بعد ذلك: ثم استوى إلى السماء وهي دخان فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r16.claim: سمك means the sky’s height, described as extending five hundred years.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r16.anchor: رفع سمكها: أي جعل مقدارها بها في العلو مديدا رفيعا مقدار خمسمائة عام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r17.claim: The sky was made smooth without high or low places, or alternatively completed and perfected in construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r17.anchor: فسواها: أي جعلها ملساء مستوية، ليس فيها مرتفع ولا منخفض، أو تممها وأتقن إنشاءها
